# 115 · HoldDocument.idempotencyKey renamed, the query strings not: a retried POST holds the seats twice

[← All examples](../README.md)

| Verdict | Categories | Severity if shipped | Change | Verified unit | Approach |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **✗ Violation: 5 boundary changes** | functional | high | refactor, behaviour change not intended | [`HoldDocument`](../../examples/apps/boxoffice/ticketing-service/src/main/java/net/terminalvalue/boxoffice/ticketing/store/HoldDocument.java) | [B12: Boundary contracts](../../lib/README.md) |

> The developer renames `HoldDocument.idempotencyKey` to `requestKey`; the IDE renames the component and its javadoc, the hold is built positionally, so nothing else changes and everything compiles. The mapper now stores the key under `requestKey`, while `TicketingStore.holdByIdempotencyKey` still runs `where("idempotencyKey")` and the unique index is still on `idempotencyKey`: the lookup matches nothing, the index covers nothing, and a client that retries `POST /concerts/{id}/holds` with the same `Idempotency-Key` gets a second hold on other seats. The boundary contract's stored types block shows the document's shape and checks every field-name string in the module against it; the regenerated contract has three new `!` lines under `HoldDocument`.

Tags: [spring-boot](../README.md#tag-spring-boot), [idempotency](../README.md#tag-idempotency), [schema-drift](../README.md#tag-schema-drift), [contract-diff-review](../README.md#tag-contract-diff-review)

## The change

Rename the record component `idempotencyKey` of `HoldDocument` to `requestKey`, with its `@param` line. The component is set positionally by `HoldService.hold` and its accessor is called nowhere, so the rename touches one file; the three strings in `TicketingStore` that name the field (`where("idempotencyKey")` in `holdByIdempotencyKey`, and the unique index on `customerId, idempotencyKey` with its partial filter in the constructor) are strings, which the IDE does not rename.

**Before** ([`HoldDocument.java`](../../examples/apps/boxoffice/ticketing-service/src/main/java/net/terminalvalue/boxoffice/ticketing/store/HoldDocument.java), line 9):

```java
 * A customer's claim on some seats until {@code expiresAt}. The seats themselves record whether the claim still
 * stands; this document only remembers what was asked for and what it costs.
 *
 * @param idempotencyKey the client's {@code Idempotency-Key}, if it sent one
 */
@Document("holds")
public record HoldDocument(
    // ...
        long amountCents,
        Instant createdAt,
        Instant expiresAt,
        String idempotencyKey) {}
```

**After:**

```java
 * A customer's claim on some seats until {@code expiresAt}. The seats themselves record whether the claim still
 * stands; this document only remembers what was asked for and what it costs.
 *
 * @param requestKey the client's {@code Idempotency-Key}, if it sent one
 */
@Document("holds")
public record HoldDocument(
    // ...
        long amountCents,
        Instant createdAt,
        Instant expiresAt,
        String requestKey) {}
```

## What the verifier found

The module's boundaries differ from their contract in 5 lines:

| Bean | The contract has | The bytecode now has |
|---|---|---|
| `stored net.terminalvalue.boxoffice.ticketing.store.HoldDocument` | *(nothing)* | `! TicketingStore(MongoTemplate) indexes "idempotencyKey": not a field of HoldDocument, OrderDocument or SeatDocument, so the index is on a field that is never set` |
| `stored net.terminalvalue.boxoffice.ticketing.store.HoldDocument` | *(nothing)* | `! TicketingStore(MongoTemplate) queries "idempotencyKey": not a field of HoldDocument, OrderDocument or SeatDocument, so the condition tests a field that is never set` |
| `stored net.terminalvalue.boxoffice.ticketing.store.HoldDocument` | *(nothing)* | `! TicketingStore.holdByIdempotencyKey(String, String) queries "idempotencyKey": not a field of HoldDocument, so the condition tests a field that is never set` |
| `stored net.terminalvalue.boxoffice.ticketing.store.HoldDocument` | *(nothing)* | `requestKey: String` |
| `stored net.terminalvalue.boxoffice.ticketing.store.HoldDocument` | `idempotencyKey: String` | *(removed)* |

A line is a route, listener, schedule, bean definition or configuration key, the advice on a member, a property of a wire type, or a `!` line where an annotation does not do what it says; a member's line changes with its signature and parameter annotations.

## Would the existing tests have caught it?

No: every existing unit test passes (`:ticketing-service:test`, run against the patched code).

## Why it matters

Spring Data writes a document from the record through its mapping: after the rename a new hold is stored with a `requestKey` field and no `idempotencyKey`. The reads go through strings that the mapper passes to the database as they are when they match no property: `where("customerId").is(c).and("idempotencyKey").is(k)` now asks for a field no hold has, so `holdByIdempotencyKey` returns empty for every key, `HoldService.hold` sees no earlier hold and takes new seats, and the unique partial index on `(customerId, idempotencyKey)`, the second line of defence against a double hold, indexes a field that is never set and rejects nothing. A client that retries the request after a timeout (the reason the header exists) holds and pays for two sets of seats. No compiler, no startup check and no unit test with a mocked store notices: the strings are valid field names as far as the driver is concerned, and the system test's idempotent retry needs Docker.

## Why the verdict is right

The stored types block of the boundary contract lists each `@Document` of the module as the mapper stores it (`stored net.terminalvalue.boxoffice.ticketing.store.HoldDocument: record, collection "holds"`, then `_id: String (id)`, `concertId: String`, ..., `idempotencyKey: String`) and checks every string the module's code passes as a field name (`Criteria.where` and `and`, the `Update` operators, `Index.on`, `Sort.by`, projections, repository `@Query` documents, `@CompoundIndex` definitions) against the documents the method names (`HoldDocument.class` passed to the template, or the document it instantiates; a helper that names none takes its callers' documents). The change is a refactoring, so the runner regenerates the contract and the reviewer reads the diff: under `HoldDocument` the line `idempotencyKey: String` becomes `requestKey: String`, and three `!` lines appear: `TicketingStore(MongoTemplate) queries "idempotencyKey": not a field of HoldDocument, OrderDocument or SeatDocument, so the condition tests a field that is never set` (the partial filter of the index, in the constructor that names all three documents), `TicketingStore(MongoTemplate) indexes "idempotencyKey": not a field of HoldDocument, OrderDocument or SeatDocument, so the index is on a field that is never set`, and `TicketingStore.holdByIdempotencyKey(String, String) queries "idempotencyKey": not a field of HoldDocument, so the condition tests a field that is never set`. The new `!` lines are the violation.

## What to do

Rename the three strings too (`where("requestKey")`, `.on("requestKey", ASC)`, `where("requestKey").exists(true)`), or keep the stored name with `@Field("idempotencyKey") String requestKey`, which also keeps the holds already in the database readable. Either way the regenerated contract has no `!` line under `HoldDocument`, and with `@Field` its shape line reads `idempotencyKey: String (requestKey)`: the stored name unchanged, the Java name beside it, which is the diff a reviewer approves. The rename without `@Field` also orphans the existing documents' `idempotencyKey` values, which the contract does not see; that is a data migration, and the reviewer's next question.

## Notes

- The first example of the stored types block of a boundary contract (`lib/src/store.rs`): the shape of each Spring Data MongoDB document as the mapping layer writes it (the `@Id` or the property named `id` as `_id`, a `@Field` rename as `due: Instant (dueAt)`, `@Transient` and `transient` fields left out, embedded local types as their own `record, embedded` blocks), and under each document a `!` line for every string in the module that names a field it does not have. The strings come from the bytecode: the constant pushed as the field argument of `Criteria.where`/`and`, the `Update` operators (`set`, `unset`, `inc`, `push`, `pull`, `rename`, ...), `Index.on`, `Sort.by` (varargs read back from the array the compiler builds), `Sort.Order.asc`/`desc`, the projection's `include`/`exclude`, and from the annotations: a repository method's `@Query` (`value`, `sort`, `fields`, parsed as the loose JSON Spring accepts, with the `$` operators transparent) and a document's `@CompoundIndex(def)`.
- A string names a property by its Java name or its stored name, as Spring's query mapper accepts both (`where("due")` and `where("dueAt")` both reach a `@Field("due") Instant dueAt`), `_id` and the id property's own name both reach the id, a dotted path goes through an embedded type's fields, through a collection or array to its element and through a map to any key, and stops at a leaf: `"assignee.email" is a String, which has no fields`. `$`-segments (`steps.$.done`) and array indices are skipped. The nearest property is suggested when one is within a few edits (`not a field of NoteDocument (createdAt?)`); here `requestKey` is too far from `idempotencyKey` for a hint. The library's Spring fixtures (`lib/tests/fixtures/spring/fixtures/spring/NotesStore.java`, `NoteRepository.java`, `TaskDocument.java`) have one wrong string of each kind.
- Which document a string is about is read from the method: the document classes it passes to the template or instantiates. `holdByIdempotencyKey` names `HoldDocument.class` alone, so its line says `not a field of HoldDocument`; the constructor creates indexes for `SeatDocument`, `HoldDocument` and `OrderDocument`, so the two lines from it name all three (the string is a field of none), and the line goes under the first. A private helper that names no document (`makeAvailable()` in the same store) takes the documents of the methods that call it. The checks cover Spring Data MongoDB; JPA queries are JPQL, which Hibernate validates at startup, and derived query methods (`findByHoldId`) are checked by Spring Data at startup, so neither needs a contract line. Aggregation pipelines are not followed: a stage after a `group` names computed fields.
- The three Box Office modules with documents gained stored types blocks with this feature (ticketing-service 4, payment-service 1, messaging 2) and no `!` line: every one of their forty-odd field strings resolves, including `where("_id")` on `PaymentDocument`, whose id property is `orderId`, and `Sort.by("_id")` on the outbox. The example renames the one field that only strings read, so that the whole breakage is in the strings; a rename of `SeatDocument.label` would break the hold itself (every hold conflicts, which a test sees at once), while this one breaks only the retry.
- The patch changes the Java of the module, so the runner compiles it with Gradle, reads the runtime class path through the build's `printRuntimeClasspath` task, and runs `jvmcontract update` then `verify` with `--resources` and `--classpath`. The Spring Boot tests of the module need Docker for Testcontainers; without it they fail before the change is tested, which the page records as the tests' result, not the verifier's.
- The observation specs (`jvmcontract observations --against`, foundations O2), Box Office with this change against Box Office as it is (`lib/tests/observations.rs`, `box_office_examples_compare_as_their_boundary_diffs_say`): `POST /concerts/{id}/holds` gets one changed obligation, its `MongoTemplate.insert` effect: the payload no longer snapshots `objectToSave.idempotencyKey` and now snapshots `objectToSave.requestKey`. The query strings that still name the old field are reads, which the spec models as calls and doesn't observe (`observations::NOT_OBSERVED`); the stored-types block of the boundary contract checks them.

**Provenance:** Constructed from the Spring Data MongoDB gotcha that the field names in Criteria, Update, Index and Sort are strings the mapper passes through when they match no property, so an IDE rename of a record component leaves every query of the old name valid, silent and empty. Chosen on the Box Office hold's idempotency key because the only readers of the field are those strings.
